name: Caskwright
description: A small distillery on the edge of the moor. Four casks at a time, bottled at cask strength, sold at the door.
canvasAlt: A warm rust-coloured glow moving slowly across near-black, like firelight on a barrel end

sections.heading: Four casks at a time
sections.body: Caskwright sits on the edge of the moor, in a stone shed that used to hold tractors. We fill four casks at a time and bottle them one by one.

sections.heading: Barley from the next valley
sections.body: Floor malted, milled coarse, and mashed in an open tun so you can smell the wash from the road. Nothing is rushed to hit a delivery date.

sections.heading: One copper pot, run slow
sections.body: A slow run keeps the heavier oils in the spirit, which is what gives it weight later. We cut early and lose some volume for it.

sections.heading: Time is the only ingredient we cannot buy
Ex-bourbon, then a year in oloroso
sections.body: The first fill gives vanilla and coconut, the second gives dried fruit and a darker colour. We taste every cask before we decide it is finished.

sections.heading: Cask strength, never chill filtered
sections.body: Each bottle is numbered by hand and carries the cask it came from. Add water at the table if you want it softer, rather than us doing it for you.

sections.heading: The door is open on Saturdays
sections.body: Come and taste what is in the tun. If a cask is ready you can fill a bottle from it and write your own label.
